title: Bidirectional tanka seam-contrastive dataset
purpose: Convert the six machine-clear bidirectional tanka in v1.24 into a contrastive seam dataset that exposes how identical 31-kana material supports 5/7/5/7/7 segmentation in both reading directions without being a self-palindrome.

metrical_geometry.finding: For a 31-kana tanka segmented 5/7/5/7/7 in both directions, the reverse segmentation maps to 7/14/19/26 in forward coordinates. Every internal reverse boundary is shifted exactly +2 kana from the corresponding forward boundary.
metrical_geometry.interpretation: The bidirectional form supplies a historical contrastive lattice in which lexical/syntactic seams must be able to re-form across a systematic two-kana boundary shift.

strict_palindrome_generator.reason: The six records are deliberately non-self-palindromic.

seam_model.use: Score whether candidate material can support plausible alternative lexical boundaries near the 5/7/5/7/7 seam positions, without treating the bidirectional corpus as positive strict-palindrome text.

future_bidirectional_mode.structural_contract: 31 kana; forward and exact reverse both independently segment 5/7/5/7/7; forward != reverse

safety_rules: Do not count v1.28 cases as strict palindrome positives.
Do not infer lexical boundaries solely from the +2 geometry; the geometry is metrical, while lexical/syntactic boundaries require source-specific review.
Retain forward and reverse provenance separately.
Do not inject bidirectional source strings into the public candidate pool.
The +2 seam signature is a structural consequence of the meter and length, not by itself evidence of linguistic naturalness.
next_action: Use v1.28 as a seam-contrastive research fixture. Before enabling any score or generator rule, test whether known positive strict families and known negative controls differ meaningfully on local boundary-shift lexical support.
